items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The agent had told the man who owned the club that we were an item, we were together... The drummer would be a girl, the piano player would be a crazy man and me... Walter got it off on me.

ctx.x: How long did you work in Jackson? How long was this gig?

I'd say I lived in Jackson for about a year, and then my brother brought me to California. I got to California when I was 20, and I couldn't work night clubs until I was 21. So, when I became 21, an agent named Johnnie Robinson, I described him in the story, he used to walk on his toes a little bit and with his mischievous smile on his face, with his ruddy cheeks, and he used to book a piano player and a drummer and a singer. The drummer would be a girl, the piano player would be a crazy man and me, and I'd stand…

High," and I used that incident as -- sure is a noisy house. "On the edge of his tongue he dared not speak father to mother, young and adultness going to and from school, it was spewed out windows of cars to me cruising the neighborhood as I was calling home thusly, want a ride.
